Title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
Content: Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. Location Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu User Setting 3D Gizmo Divided Gizmo Operation Move Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Move by dragging in a desired direction. Note: Move Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. Move X Axis Click &gt Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. Move Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. Rotate Follow the indicated guideline below: Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) 'E' on keyboard The Gizmo appears. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). Click Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. Note: Rotate Y Axis Click &gt Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. Rotate X Axis Click &gt Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. Rotate Z Axis Click &gt Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis.
ContentDescription: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide for using the Gizmo tool to move and rotate patterns, objects, and avatar joints in a 3D environment.

Title: Reverse Arrangement Horizontally/Vertically
Content: Objective Flip 3D Garment Patterns horizontally and vertically while maintaining its curvature. Note: Flipping Patterns while maintaining its curvature is only applicable for patterns arranged with Arrangement Points. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reverse-Arrange Horizontally / Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reverse-Arrange Horizontally / Vertically The selected Pattern is now being flipped over horizontally/vertically while maintaining its curvature.
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly flip 3D garment patterns horizontally and vertically while preserving their curvature using the 3D Toolbar and right-click pop-up menu for precise arrangement."

Title: Flip Horizontally/Vertically
Content: Objective Flip a Pattern horizontally or vertically in the 3D window. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically The selected Pattern is now being rotated 180 on the Y axis (vertically) or X axis (horizontally).
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for flipping a pattern horizontally or vertically in the 3D window using the 3D toolbar and right-click pop-up menu.

Title: Reset 2D Arrangement
Content: Objective Spread and arrange the entire or the selected patterns in the 3D window identical to 2D window state. Location Selected Pattern 3D Toolbar Select/Move right-click menu on a 3D pattern Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) All Pattern Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) Operation Selected Pattern Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement identical to 2D window state. Note: Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move right-click menu on a 3D pattern Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) The selected Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state. All Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) The entire Pattern is now being rearranged to match 2D window state.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on how to reset the arrangement of 3D patterns to match their corresponding 2D window states, allowing for seamless pattern management and design adjustments.

Title: Fold Arrangement
Content: Objective Fold Seam Allowances, collars and cuffs before activating the Simulation for better stability. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar Fold Arrangement Operation After arranging Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Fold Arrangement 3D Toolbar Fold Arrangement The entire Internal Line/Shape of a 3D Garment appears. Click on an Internal Line/Shape to fold. The folding Gizmo appears. Rotate the red or green axis along the blue circle as desired. The selected area's Pattern is now being folded accordingly. If the pattern is symmetrical, it is folded symmetrically. (ver 11) Note: Folding Internal Line/Shape is also available after simulating/draping the Garment.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to effectively fold seam allowances, collars, and cuffs in a 3D garment simulation for enhanced stability and accurate pattern arrangement.

Title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
Content: Objective Arrangement Points are created based on the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. Note: Precise arrangement is available by using Gizmo or Property Editor even after arranging with Arrangement Points. Location Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points Operation Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display Show Arrangement Points The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). Select a desired Arrangement Point. The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). Note: Flip Wrap Direction Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window Click Flip Wrap Direction to flip its direction.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to create and manipulate Arrangement Points around an Avatar using Bounding Volumes, ensuring precise pattern placement and symmetry through intuitive controls.

Title: Move with Arrow Keys (3D)
Content: Objective Select Patterns in the 3D window, then use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move them in specific increments. Location Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Set Specific Movement Increment Main Menu Preferences Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Operation Move Patterns with Arrow Keys Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Select/Move 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Patterns or trims in the 3D window. Selected Patterns or trims are highlighted in yellow. Use the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected Pattern or trim. Arrow Keys Description Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive y-axis. The Garment moves upwards. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative y-axis. The Garment moves downwards. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative x-axis. The Garment moves to the left. Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive x-axis. The Garment moves to the right. + Ctrl Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the negative z-axis. The Garment moves away from you. + Ctrl Move selected Patterns or trims along or towards the positive z-axis. The Garment moves towards you. Set Specific Movement Increment Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Preferences Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 3D Window) Grid Properties Property Editor 3D Arrow Key Movement Enter the desired distance moved with each arrow key input.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a guide on how to select and precisely move patterns in a 3D environment using keyboard arrow keys and customizable movement increments.

Title: Arrangement Property Setting
Content: Objective Set arrangement property details after arranging patterns with Arrangement Points. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Note: The arrangement properties are only accessible for Patterns that are arranged by Arrangement Points. Operation Arrange Patterns with Arrangement Points Follow the guidelines below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select 3D Pattern Property Editor Arrangement Point Name Shows which arrangement point the selected pattern is on top of. Shape Style Changes the arrangement bounding volume pattern to be flat or curved. Position X Moves horizontally according to the arrangement bounding volume. Position Y Moves vertically according to the arrangement bounding volume. Offset Adjusts the offset and curvature between the arrangement bounding volume and the pattern. Orientation Changes the pattern's direction according to the arrangement bounding volume.
ContentDescription: This web page provides detailed instructions for managing arrangement properties of patterns using Arrangement Points in the 3D Toolbar.

Title: Reset 3D Arrangement
Content: Objective Return arrangement of the entire or selected Patterns back to pre-simulation state in the 3D window. Use this function when draping is not functioning properly after arranging around the Avatar. Location Selected Pattern 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected) All Pattern Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 3D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 3D Arrangement (All) Operation Selected Pattern Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement. Note: Press the Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected) The selected Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state. All Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 3D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 3D Arrangement (All) The entire Pattern is now being rearranged back to pre-simulation state.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on resetting the arrangement of selected or all 3D patterns back to their pre-simulation state to resolve draping issues in the 3D window.

Title: Direct Positioning
Content: Objective Activate Direct Positioning to click to easily arrange Patterns and OBJs. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click 3D Pattern or OBJ Direct Positioning Operation Follow the path: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click 3D Pattern or OBJ Direct Positioning Hover the mouse over a Garment or Avatar. The selected Pattern or OBJ moves along with the mouse cursor. Click to place the Pattern in the desired location. Note: When arranging Patterns, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to restrict Pattern rotation (ver4.0.0).
ContentDescription: This web page provides a streamlined guide for using the Direct Positioning feature in the 3D Toolbar to effortlessly arrange Patterns and OBJs by clicking and dragging them into desired locations.

Title: Smart Arrangement
Content: Objective Arrange a new Pattern onto an existing Pattern while maintaining 3D draping state (ver3.0.0). Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement Operation Utilizing the sewing tools, sew a new Pattern to an existing Pattern that is being draped. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Smart Arrangement The selected Pattern is now being arranged to where it is sewn as draped.
ContentDescription: "Learn how to seamlessly arrange and sew a new pattern onto an existing draped pattern using the 3D Toolbar and Smart Arrangement features."

Title: Fold Pattern
Content: Objective Use this function to create a pressing effect by adjusting the angle of Pattern's Internal Line, for instance, pressed lines of formal trousers, fold direction of pleats. Location Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Operation Click on an Internal Line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Pattern Property Editor Fold Fold Angle Adjust the value of Fold Angle as desired. Note: Fold Strength Sets the angle closer as the value increases. The value range is in between 0 to 20. Fold Angle Sets the value in the range of 0 to 360, 180 represents a flat state. The internal line is folded towards the front of the pattern as the fold angle is closer to 0, and is folded into the back of the pattern as the angle is closer to 360. Fold Rendering Sets whether the pleats to have soft or sharp edges according to user preference. (Only applicable if Fold Arrangement is used on an Internal line.)
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the Pattern Property Editor to create realistic pressing effects on garment patterns by adjusting the fold angle and strength of internal lines.

Title: Curved Side Geometry
Content: Objective Apply and adjust curvature on edges of Patterns for more natural and realistic look (ver2.2.0). Location 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Operation Firstly, change the 3D Garment rendering style to Thick Textured Surface in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern / Edit Pattern Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express curved sided effect. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Enter a desired value at: Property Editor Selected Line Curved Side Geometry Curvature (%) The curvature is now being applied according to the entered value. Note: The maximum Curvature (%) value is 50 percent (%) of the fabric thickness. For instance, if the fabric thickness is being set at 1mm, the maximum Curvature (%) is 0.5mm.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for applying and adjusting curvature on pattern edges to achieve a more natural and realistic appearance in 3D garment rendering.

Title: Bond
Content: Objective Add bonding effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond Operation Select a pattern or an internal shape to express bonding with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Bond The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent orange color. By default, the same physical property as the selected Pattern/Internal Shape is now being added to the selected Pattern/Internal Shape. Activate the Simulate. The bonded area is now being displayed stiffer as if an interlining has been fused. Repeat the first step again. In the Property Editor, select a desired preset to change its physical property. For more detailed adjustments, click on Detail. The lists on the drop-down menu are the same as Fabric's.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply bonding effects to selected patterns and internal shapes using the Property Editor in version 2.3.0.

Title: Skive
Content: Objective Add skiving effect on desired parts of a Pattern or all Patterns (ver2.3.0). Location Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Skive Operation Select a pattern or an internal shape to express skiving with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor (Internal Shapes/Pattern Only) Bond/Skive Skive The select Pattern/Internal Shape is now being displayed in a semi-transparent grey color. A scrollbar appears, displaying the physical property of the pattern from the value range of zero ('0') to one hundred ('100') in Percentage (%). Move the scrollbar to adjust as desired. Activate the Simulate. The area of the internal shape is now being displayed softer as if it has been shaved down.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on adding a skiving effect to selected patterns or internal shapes using the Property Editor in version 2.3.0.

Title: Express Air Pressure
Content: Objective Use the Pressure value to create an effect of air or padded materials such as padded jumpers, pillows, cushions, balloons, etc. Location Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Pressure Operation Select a Pattern to express pressure with Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern tools. Its properties appear in Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Simulation Properties Pressure Adjust the value as desired.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on using the Pressure value in the Pattern Property Editor to simulate the appearance and behavior of air-filled or padded materials in design applications.

Title: Elastic
Content: Objective Insert elastic to the outer/internal lines of a Pattern to express shirring details. Location Pattern Property Editor Select a Line Elastic Operation Select a outer or internal line with Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool. Follow the indicated guideline: Pattern Property Editor Select a Line Elastic Click the checkbox and set it On. Adjust the intensity and ratio of the elastic. Note: Elastic Properties Elastic Decides whether to insert an elastic or not. Even though adjusting the value of intensity and ratio is not going to be applied, if this is not being checked. Strength Increase or decrease the elastic intensity value. Even if elastic that has the same ratio, may be affected differently depending on their intensity. Ratio Shows the elastic ratio when the selected segment is set at 100%. Various garment can be expressed by adjusting the elastic ratio. The elastic ratio can be set up to 200% of the maximum segment. Length Adjusts the elastic when the length value is entered. If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied to each segment. Entire Length If multiple segments are selected, the entered value will be applied as the total length of the combined segments.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to insert and adjust elastic details in garment patterns using the Pattern Property Editor.

Title: Use Layer (Drape Additional Garment)
Content: Objective This function allows easier simulation when setting which layer to get in/outward among overlapped multiple layers. By using this function, taking out inaccurately inwardly simulated patterns such as pockets and buttons, gets easier. In addition, adding additional outerwear on top of garments such as dress and shirts. The default layer value of zero ('0') means the layer function is being off. In that state, the arrangement order of the patterns gets decided. Location Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer Operation Select a pattern in the 3D window to set a layer with Select/Move tool. Note: Select patterns in the 2D window, in case of having difficulties when choosing in the 3D window. Follow the guide below: Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Layer Apply the value by clicking Simulate button. Note: When the layer value is being set, the patterns become highlighted in blue outline. Once the draping in desired order is completed, set the value back to zero ('0') for more stable simulation. (There is no change in draping even after modifying the value back to zero('0')). If the layer value is zero('0'), but the menu appears in red when all patterns are being selected, it is because there is a variety of values being mixed. Therefore revert the layer value to zero('0') once again. Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu Show/Hide Color (Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1) to hide the layered patterns outline highlight color in the 3D window. Show layer Depth (Ver. 2024.1) Objective Toggle view option in the 2D window to display the layer number and color code to help visualize layers. Location 2D Window 2D Information Show Pattern Layer Operation Follow the guideline for Apply Layer Value to number different pattern layers: Select and enter desired Layer number on selected pattern or multiple patterns. Layer value is assigned Set different layer values for other patterns. Click the Show Pattern Layer option under 2D information icon to activate. Number of layer will be indicated and patterns with the same layer will be the same color Click the Show Pattern Layer option again to inactivate it. Note: The color values for each layer are as follows. Layer 0 has one unique color: Light Gray Layers 1 to 23 each have different color values. This repeats from 24 onwards. Negative Layers are applied in the reverse order of positive numbers. Layer depth display will automatically turn off when switching to another 2D Pattern Rendering Style. End Result Quickly visualizing and controlling layers is now convenient and intuitive
ContentDescription: This web page provides a comprehensive guide to efficiently manage and simulate overlapping pattern layers in garment design, ensuring accurate representation and manipulation of complex designs.

Title: Shrink Pattern
Content: Objective Shrink or stretch 3D Garment Pattern horizontally and vertically without changing it in the 2D Pattern window. The default value is 100 percent (%) which indicates the natural state of the Garment material, in other words there is no artificial shrinkage or stretchiness. Use the function to express shrinkage after textile treatments such as garment washing, or use it temporarily to draw the inner layer against the avatar when dressing multiple layers of Garments for easier Simulation. Location Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Shrinkage Weft/Warp Operation Select a Pattern to shrink with 2D toolbar's Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Pattern Property Editor Simulation Properties Shrinkage Weft/Warp Enter desired shrink values. The Pattern in the 3D window is now being shrunk accordingly.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a guide on how to adjust the horizontal and vertical dimensions of 3D garment patterns without altering their 2D representations, enabling users to simulate fabric shrinkage or stretch for accurate garment fitting and layering.

Title: Particle Distance Setting
Content: Objective Particle Distance refers to the average distance between the points that make up a Garment Pattern, in other words, size of the mesh. The Garment quality and Simulation speed depend on the Particle Distance. Therefore set the value at 20mm when making a Garment and dressing it on an Avatar for faster working process, and set it under 5mm to enhance the Garment quality once it is completed. Location Property Editor Simulation Properties Particle Distance Operation Select Pattern(s). Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Simulation Properties Particle Distance Input desired value for the Particle Distance. (Minimum '0.8' to maximum '700.0') Press Enter on keyboard to apply.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidelines for setting the Objective Particle Distance in garment simulation to optimize both quality and speed during the design process.

Title: Remeshing
Content: Objective Generates aligned automatic Retopology results. (MD 8) Location Right click on a pattern (3D window) Remeshing Right click on a pattern (3D window) Mesh Style Quad (Grid) (ver. 2024.0) Pattern property window Remeshing Pattern property window Mesh Mesh Style Quad (Grid) (ver. 2024.0) Operation Find and click the menu indicated in Location. The mesh of the selected pattern is rearranged in an aligned quad mesh. When changing pattern's particle distance, it will be reflected to re-meshed pattern. When rotating a pattern in a 2D window, the meshes are rearranged relative to the X, Y axis of the 2D window. - After rotating pattern in 2D window, need to Undo Remeshing and apply Remeshing again to reflect the direction of the meshes.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on achieving aligned automatic retopology results in 3D modeling, focusing on remeshing techniques and mesh style adjustments.

Title: Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh
Content: Objective Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures. Note: Please refer to the below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. As the program speed may differ due to their intrinsic characteristics, please select the most appropriate Mesh Type based on your needs. To use our program most efficiently, however, we strongly suggest you set all Pattern Mesh to Triangular when editing 3D Garments. Then, change ONLY the necessary Patterns' Mesh type to Quadrangular to complete the Garment. When to Use Triangular Mesh: All Cases, except for exceptional cases, needed to use Quadrangular Mesh. When to Use Quadrangular Mesh: When a detail of a 3D Garment needs to round smoothly, such as a shirt collar or piping. Location Right click on a pattern (3D window) Triangulate/Quadrangulate Right click on a pattern (3D window) Mesh Style Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) (ver. 2024.0) Pattern Property Editor Miscellaneous Mesh Typ Quad / Triangle Pattern Property Editor Mesh Mesh Style Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) (ver. 2024.0) Note: Improved the algorithm for the Rectangle (Optimize) feature. (ver. 2024.0)
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on converting synchronized 3D garment designs into optimized quadrangular or triangular mesh structures, emphasizing the most efficient usage of mesh types based on garment details.

Title: Show 3D Line Length
Content: Objective Confirm the difference in lengths of the selected Pattern when simulated in the 3D window. Location Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 2D Pattern Edit Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern 2D Toolbar Edit Pattern or Transform Pattern Select the desired line on the 2D window. Respective properties appear in the Property Editor. See the 3D line length by following the indicated path: Property Editor Selected Line 3D Line Length
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide to confirm and view the 3D lengths of selected patterns within a 2D editing interface.

Title: Auto Fitting
Content: Create Fitting Suit Objective Create a Fitting Suit for a custom avatar for Auto Fitting. Create a Fitting Suit Reference Line along the avatar surface and apply Fitting Suit. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Create Fitting Suit 3D Toolbar Create Fitting Suit Operation 1. Load your custom avatar. 2. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 3. Create Fitting Suit Reference Line following the guide of dialogue and mouse pointer. When you have finished creating the lines, the preview of the Fitting Suit appears. 4. After creating all reference lines, press Apply button. Fitting Suit is simulated on the avatar. 5. Press Save button to save the avatar. It is saved as an avatar file(.avt) including Fitting Suit data. Note If you do not want to create symmetry, turn off Symmetry settings. If you want to recreate the reference line, select the reference line in the dialogue and press the Delete button. Auto Fitting / Re-target Draping Objective Auto Fitting Automatically adjust the size of your garment to your custom avatar and simulate the garment. Re-target Draping Simulate garment on your custom avatar. (This function maintains its original size) Location Auto Fitting Main Menu 2D Pattern Fitting Auto Fitting 2D Toolbar Auto Fitting Re-target Draping Main Menu 3D Garment Re-target Draping 3D Toolbar Re-target Draping Operation 1. Load the avatar which has completed the Create Fitting Suit process. 2. Add the garment which has Fitting Suit data. - The garment simulated on the avatar provided by Marvelous Designer (Marvelous Designer 9.5 or above) - The garment simulated on the avatar having Fitting Suit data after doing Create Fitting Suit. 3. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 4. Adjust the below options as needed in the popup window, and click OK. Maintain Pattern Curvature (%) Set the extent of deformation of pattern curvature. * Higher values will deform only the size of the pattern while preserving the existing curvature, while lower values will deform both the size and curvature of the pattern. Maintain Graphic Size ON Graphics maintain their size after auto fitting OFF The graphic is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. Maintain Texture Size ON Textures maintain their size after auto fitting OFF The Texture is automatically resized based on the size changes of the patters. Auto Fitting The size of the garment is automatically adjusted and the garment is simulated on your custom avatar. Re-target Draping The garment maintains its size, uv, textures and is simulated on your custom avatar. Note Before you press the Menu button, increase the particle distance of the 3D garment, which will help this function run faster. Before you press Menu button, change the property of the 3D garment to its default, which will help this function run efficiently. Show Avatar Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of an avatar fitting suit View icons on the 3D window Avatar Display Show Avatar Fitting Suit Show Garment Fitting Suit (Above ver. 11) Please follow the below to see the details of a garment fitting suit View icons on the 3D window 3D Garment Display Show Garment Fitting Suit
ContentDescription: "Create and apply a custom Fitting Suit for your avatar to ensure seamless auto fitting and accurate garment simulation in a 3D environment."

Title: Press
Content: Objective Use this function to create pressing effect especially for the edges of two layers sewn together. Location Main Menu 3D Garment Press 3D Toolbar Press Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Press 3D Toolbar Press Click on one of the Pattern layers to press. The selected Pattern is now being transparent. Click on the other layer. All Sewing Lines on the selected Pattern switched to Turned Sewing Line Type (ver4.1.0). The Pattern selected first appears again. Activate the Simulate. The bulging edges are now being flattened.
ContentDescription: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for utilizing the 3D Garment Press tool to create a pressing effect on the edges of sewn pattern layers.

Title: Solidify
Content: Objective Maintain desired draping state per pattern unit. For instance, solidify creases on the back of the knee area of a pair of jeans to maintain its shape while simulating (Ver 2.5.0). Location 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu Solidify Operation 3D Toolbar Select a 3D Pattern with Select/Move tool. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Right-click Pop-up Menu Solidify The selected Pattern is now being solidified. Follow the indicated guideline and adjust the Strength: Click Pattern Property Editor Bond/Skive Solidify Strength The selected Pattern's 3D shape is now being solidified according to the Strength value. Note: 3D Statement The higher the Strength value, the better the sustenance. Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu Show/Hide Color (Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1) to hide the Solidify color display in the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides instructions for solidifying the draping state of 3D garment patterns, ensuring shape maintenance and crease definition, particularly in areas like the back of the knee for jeans.

Title: Flip Normal
Content: Objective Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. Location Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Pattern Flip Normal Operation Select Select/Move tool. Select a Pattern to flip. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Pattern Flip Normal The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. Note: Fold Angle value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).
ContentDescription: "Effortlessly flip the fabric surface of your patterns before or after draping to optimize your sewing workflow and save time."

Title: Freeze/Unfreeze
Content: Objective Use this function to fasten Patterns like solid objects. For example, deactivated Patterns do not collide during Simulation however, frozen Patterns do. Therefore it is better to use it for draping multiple layered Garments. For instance, draping and freezing inner Garments first, then draping outerwear simultaneously, solves the occasional instabilities. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Freeze / Unfreeze The selected Pattern is now being frozen/unfrozen. Note: 3D Statement Right-click to open the 3D Background Options Menu Show/Hide Color (Show/Hide 3D Color Ver. 2024.1) to hide the Freeze color display in the 3D window.
ContentDescription: This web page provides guidance on using the Freeze/Unfreeze function to effectively manage the simulation of layered garments in 3D and 2D environments, enhancing stability during draping.

Title: Deactivate(Pattern & Sewing)/Activate
Content: Objective Deactivated Patterns are considered as nonexistence in the 3D window. Therefore the rest of the Patterns simulate through the deactivated Patterns. The function is generally used to keep complicated details such as pleats or slits, from avoiding collapsing (ver2.3.0). Note: When deactivating certain Patterns, the Simulation speed gets faster as it excludes them from calculation. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate 2D Toolbar Transform Pattern 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu Deactivate (Pattern &amp Sewing) / Activate The selected Patterns and connected Sewing Lines are now being deactivated/activated. Title: Copy/Paste Patterns (3D)
Content: Objective Copy and paste patterns in the 3D window. Location Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Copy or Paste Operation Select the Select/Move tool from the 3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) Copy or Paste A preview of the copied pattern follows the mouse cursor. Click on the desired location in the 3D window to place the duplicated pattern. The copied pattern is automatically assigned a number. Note: To copy and paste more efficiently, select the pattern, press Ctrl+C, then press Ctrl+V or Ctrl+R on the keyboard to copy, paste or mirror paste, respectively.
